name: Approval API client
description: The caller that submits an approval intent to the HTTP entry point.
reasoning_summary: The HTTP entry point requires an external caller, but the specific client implementation was outside the inspected scope.
alternative_explanations: An internal scheduler or service-to-service caller may invoke the same endpoint.
falsification_conditions: No external or internal caller can reach the entry point.
limitations: Specific client identity was not inspected.

name: POST approval entry point
description: ApprovalResource receives the approval request and delegates to ApprovalService.approve.

name: ApprovalService
description: Application service that updates approval state and writes an approval outbox record.

name: approval_outbox
description: Durable store of approval events written by ApprovalService.
limitations: Only repository migrations and a local schema snapshot were inspected.

source_locations.note: No uniqueness guard found in inspected scope.

name: Approval state and outbox transaction
description: Approval state update and outbox insert occur inside one transaction.

name: Equivalent concurrent approval requests
description: Equivalent requests may independently enter the service and reach the durable write path.
reasoning_summary: The same entry point reaches an outbox insert and no uniqueness guard was found in inspected schema sources.
alternative_explanations: An uninspected gateway may serialize equivalent requests.
A deployed schema may contain a guard absent from repository migrations.
falsification_conditions: A runtime serialization guarantee or deployed database constraint prevents the second write.
limitations: Concurrent runtime reproduction and production gateway configuration were not inspected.

source_locations.note: No uniqueness guard found in inspected scope.

name: Committed approval outbox row
description: Within the inspected producer scope, the committed outbox row is the durable representation of an approval event.
reasoning_summary: The service persists the durable event as an outbox row, and the investigation invariant candidate defines durability in terms of that row.
alternative_explanations: A separate external event log may be authoritative outside the inspected producer scope.
falsification_conditions: Another inspected or runtime source is shown to be the authoritative durable approval event.
limitations: Authority is limited to the inspected producer flow.

name: Duplicate durable writes are possible
description: Two equivalent requests can reach separate approval outbox inserts when no inspected uniqueness guard rejects the second write.
reasoning_summary: The producer path performs the durable insert, while inspected schema evidence does not show uniqueness enforcement for equivalent intents.
alternative_explanations: A production-only gateway or database rule may prevent the duplicate.
falsification_conditions: A runtime or deployed-schema guarantee prevents equivalent requests from committing two rows.
limitations: Possibility is modelled; production frequency was not measured.

source_locations.note: No uniqueness guard found in inspected scope.

name: One durable effect per approval intent
description: Equivalent requests representing one approval intent should result in one durable approval outbox record.
reasoning_summary: The approved success criterion and invariant candidate both define a single durable effect for one business intent.
alternative_explanations: The business may permit duplicate technical events if consumers deduplicate them, but that is not the approved problem definition.
falsification_conditions: The approved problem statement is revised to allow multiple durable producer records for one intent.
limitations: Business semantics are represented through the approved problem and invariant candidate rather than runtime behavior.

name: Single durable approval effect
description: One business approval intent must produce at most one committed approval outbox record.
reasoning_summary: The outbox row is the durable producer effect, and the approved semantics require one effect per intent.
alternative_explanations: The invariant could instead be enforced downstream, allowing duplicate producer records.
falsification_conditions: Approved semantics explicitly allow multiple producer records for one intent.
limitations: The current enforcement point is not established.

invariant.statement: For one business approval intent, the number of committed approval outbox rows is at most one.

name: Missing single-effect enforcement
description: The actual producer path permits a second durable write while intended behavior requires at most one.
reasoning_summary: The actual path and inspected schema do not evidence an enforcement mechanism that guarantees the intended single effect.
alternative_explanations: An uninspected production control may close the gap.
falsification_conditions: A verified production control is found that guarantees one committed row per intent.
limitations: Production-only controls remain outside inspected scope.

behavior_gap.gap_statement: No inspected enforcement prevents a second equivalent durable write.
behavior_gap.impact: One approval intent may be represented by multiple durable events.

name: Duplicate downstream processing risk
description: Multiple durable approval outbox rows can be processed as multiple approval events downstream.
reasoning_summary: The invariant candidate identifies duplicate downstream processing as the failure consequence of duplicate durable rows.
alternative_explanations: A downstream consumer may deduplicate duplicate records.
falsification_conditions: All downstream consumers are proven to deduplicate equivalent approval events.
limitations: Downstream consumers were out of scope.

name: Production controls not inspected
description: The model does not establish whether production gateway or deployed database controls differ from repository evidence.
limitations: This limitation constrains confidence but does not hide the uncertainty.
